items.heading: Here Is the Part Most
items.text: Here is the part most guidance conversations gloss over: clearing the NEET-UG cutoff gets you an MBBS seat somewhere. It does not get you a genuinely low-cost, high-quality government seat, which needs a far stronger rank.

figures.label: Academic Clinical Coursework
figures.source: 4.5 years of academic and clinical coursework, followed by a mandatory 1-year rotating internship. This is the earliest point a graduate is even eligible to register as a doctor.
figures.text: 4.5 years of academic and clinical coursework, followed by a mandatory 1-year rotating internship. This is the earliest point a graduate is even eligible to register as a doctor.

figures.label: Time Required
figures.source: For fields like cardiology, neurology, or cardiothoracic surgery, a further NEET-SS exam and 3-year super-specialisation stretches the total timeline past 12-13 years from Class 12.
figures.text: For fields like cardiology, neurology, or cardiothoracic surgery, a further NEET-SS exam and 3-year super-specialisation stretches the total timeline past 12-13 years from Class 12.

figures.label: Pay Range
figures.source: By this point, a doctor is typically 8.5-9.5 years past Class 12, and has still not reached a settled, specialist-level income.
figures.text: By this point, a doctor is typically 8.5-9.5 years past Class 12, and has still not reached a settled, specialist-level income.

figures.label: Pay Range
figures.source: Add these stages together and most doctors reach a settled, specialist-level income roughly 9-10 years after Class 12, and those who pursue DM/MCh super-specialisation, or who need more than one NEET-PG attempt, often cross 12-13 years. A family funding this path needs to plan for that entire runway, not just the 5.5-year MBBS fee.
